seed: FINDING ONE ROW IN A HUNDRED. Separating a whole screenshot puts well over a hundred pieces in the layers list, and the list shows about five rows at a time, so reaching the one you wanted is a very long scroll. The walk takes a dense capture apart, proves a find field has appeared over the list, types into it and watches a hundred rows become a handful, clicks one and watches the canvas follow, then clears it and watches the whole list come back. It also photographs the honest half of the answer: a fresh separation names every piece Text and a number, so searching it for a word you can plainly SEE on the canvas finds nothing and the list says so in as many words. Last it opens an ordinary picture with a few layers and proves there is no field there at all. It finishes by counting the threshold out loud: ten layers made by hand have no field, and fourteen do.

steps.note: a dense page as it opens: one locked Background picture and nothing else. There is no find field, because there is nothing to find

THE PROBLEM, photographed: well over a hundred pieces in a list that shows about five rows at a time. The layerList line in this stage says how many rows of what height are in how tall a viewport, which is the number the whole task is about
THE FIRST TEST: a list this long has a find field over it. It appeared on its own, because the list went past a dozen rows

THE SECOND TEST: typing narrowed the list to the rows that say it - Text 2 and Text 20 through Text 29 - and the line under the list says how many of how many. layerRowsInView below is what a person can actually see, and the FIRST result is among them: a search that narrows the list puts it back at the top, rather than leaving it parked thousands of points down where the old list was
THE THIRD TEST: a result is a row like any other. Clicking it picks the layer on the canvas, so the outline appears over the piece you were hunting for
THE FOURTH TEST: clearing the field puts the whole list back, the count line goes, and the layer you picked from the results is still the layer that is picked

THE FIFTH TEST, and the finding this walk exists to photograph: the word Recommended is on the page in front of you, and searching for it finds nothing, because a fresh separation calls every piece Text and a number. The field works; there is nothing in the rows to search. The list says so in as many words rather than going blank
THE LAST TEST: a picture with a handful of layers has no find field at all. A search box over a list you can see the whole of is a control that earns nothing, so it is not there

THE THRESHOLD, checked rather than assumed: a document somebody built by hand with ten layers in it has no find field. A search box over a list you can nearly see the whole of earns nothing, so it is not there
...and four more layers past that, the field is there. Nothing about the list changed except that it is now worth searching
